origin.description: Evaluate an approximate Hessian and gradient of a scalar function using finite differences.

arguments.name: pars
arguments.text: the numeric values of the parameters at which to evaluate the function fun and its derivatives.

arguments.name: fun
arguments.text: a function depending on the parameters pars that returns a numeric scalar.

arguments.name: .relStep
arguments.text: The relative step size to use in the finite differences. It defaults to the cube root of .Machine$double.eps.

arguments.name: minAbsPar
arguments.text: The minimum magnitude of a parameter value that is considered non-zero. It defaults to zero meaning that any non-zero value will be considered different from zero.

origin.details: This function uses a second-order response surface design known as a Koschal design to determine the parameter values at which the function is evaluated.
origin.value: A list with components mean, gradient, and Hessian. mean is fun at pars. gradient has one value per parameter. The upper triangle of Hessian is an approximate Hessian.
origin.example:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(nlme))
(fdH <- fdHess(c(12.3, 2.34), function(x) x[1]*(1-exp(-0.4*x[2]))))
stopifnot(length(fdH$ mean) == 1,
          length(fdH$ gradient) == 2,
          identical(dim(fdH$ Hessian), c(2L, 2L)))

translation.description: Evaluate an approximate Hessian and gradient of a scalar function using finite differences.

arguments.name: pars
arguments.text: the numeric values of the parameters at which to evaluate fun and its derivatives.

arguments.name: fun
arguments.text: a function of the parameters that returns a numeric scalar. Indexes are zero-based.

arguments.name: relStep
arguments.text: The relative step size. The default is the cube root of machine epsilon, which is R's .relStep.

arguments.name: minAbsPar
arguments.text: The minimum magnitude treated as non-zero. The default is zero.

translation.details: The parameter values come from a Koschal design: the center, a step along each axis in both directions, and one combined step for each pair of axes. The pure second-derivative coefficient is doubled when the transpose completes the Hessian.
translation.value: A dict with mean, gradient, and Hessian. mean is fun at pars. gradient has one value per parameter. Hessian is symmetric.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from nlme.fdhess import fdHess

result = fdHess([12.3, 2.34], lambda x: x[0] * (1 - np.exp(-0.4 * x[1])))
print(result["mean"])
print(result["gradient"])
print(result["Hessian"])
